task.title: Soften the prune advice for an ignored task ref
task.description:
internal/cli/output.go:290-299 (writeSyncResult) unconditionally tells the user to delete an ignored ref from origin: "Ignored <ref> on origin: <reason>. Prune it with: git push origin ':<ref>'".

parseOwnedRefRecords (internal/gitstore/read.go) and parseRemoteTaskHeads (internal/gitstore/sync_protocol.go) classify a ref as ignorable purely on core.ValidateTaskID(config.Key, taskID) failing. That cannot distinguish "a stranger typed junk" from "a newer Workbook version, or a second project key sharing this remote, wrote a task ID this build does not recognize".

Scenario: a future release widens the task ID format, or a second project on the same remote uses key OPS. Every older clone then prints "Ignored refs/workbook/tasks/OPS-01H... on origin: ... Prune it with: git push origin ':refs/workbook/tasks/OPS-01H...'". A user who follows the advice irreversibly deletes real append-only task history from the shared remote, against AGENTS.md ("Shared task history is append-only", "do not delete a task ref during normal operation", "Reject unknown destructive operations safely while preserving data for future versions").

Fix direction: soften the wording (for example "if this ref is not a Workbook task, remove it with ...") or gate the suggestion on a name that cannot plausibly be a task ID at all (say, one that fails the key prefix and the ULID shape rather than only the current validator).

Deferred from PR #35 (WB-01KZBT4D40T8493847N5HWMGCH) as a minor review finding; the major finding on that line, that the ref name was interpolated into the command unquoted, is fixed in commit 8739a79. This one is wording and classification, not a security defect.
